newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end up on Hong Kong reports.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end up on Hong Kong reports.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended higher on Monday, with reports in favour of Jakarta over some other Asian markets boosting sentiment on big-caps, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite index closed 6.07 points, or 0.89 percent, to 684.98 points. Advancers led decliners by 73 to 57, with 48 counters remained unchanged.

"If the Jakarta index managed to go up today while sentiment in most other Asian markets are weak, then we must be upbeat that prices may go up further," one broker with a foreign brokerage firm said.
Thornton Management (Asia) Ltd said on Monday it had reduced its weighting in the Hong Kong stock market to about 35 percent of its US$1.5 billion Asia-ex-Japan portfolio from about 40 percent.
The portfolio has been reweighted in favour of the Jakarta Stock Exchange, where a declining interest rate environment had created a positive near-term outlook, Thorton said.
Brokers said the report boosted sentiment on big-caps including Bakrie, Gudang Garam, Semen Gresik, Bank Internasional Indonesia and Barito and helped extend the index's gains.
They said active speculative buying of some secondliners, particularly in the property and textile sectors, also helped to fuel the index's rise.
Textile firms Panasia Indosyntec and Pan Brothers Tex and property firm Summarecon and Duta Pertiwi were among the gainers following the speculative buying, they said.
Matahari fell 50 rupiah to 2,850 rupiah in active trading following reports that its store in a shopping complex in central Jakarta was heavily damaged by fire, brokers said.

Commodity trading firm Prasidha ended 150 rupiah higher at 3,450 rupiah on news the firm planned to open its first powdered and instant coffee plant in March, which could boost sales, the brokers said.
